clue.text: Approaching Half Moon Street?

parts.note: the waxing moon on its way to a half moon has a curved, horn-shaped outline, and the same word names a curved row of houses in an address

explanation.surface: Directions for someone nearly at a London street named after the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Half Moon Street is a real London street, so the clue reads as directions; the moon shape that comes before a half moon, and a curved street, both carry the answer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin moon growing towards its half phase has this curved shape, and town streets built in a curve take the same name.

clue.text: Diver almost out of breath?

indicators.note: almost means the word for out of breath stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: someone out of breath is puffing

explanation.surface: A scuba diver surfacing nearly gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' reads as a person, but it is the seabird, which dives for fish; 'almost' drops the last letter G from PUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird catches fish by plunging underwater, so it is a diving bird.

clue.text: Set aside or withdrawn

explanation.surface: Something put aside, or a person who keeps to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats set aside are booked in advance, and a shy, withdrawn person is described with the same word.

clue.text: Gun in season used for bagging game mostly

indicators.note: bagging means holding in a bag, so the season word wraps around the shortened game

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: mostly means the game's name loses its last letter

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A shooting party's rifle in the hunting season, used to bag game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about shooting, but 'game' is the board game: CHESS shortened to CHES sits inside WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous make of repeating rifle, so it names a type of firearm.

clue.text: Join up, being accepted by officer with ultimate in panache

indicators.note: being accepted by means the word up is taken inside the officer-plus-letter group

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimate in points to the last letter of panache

explanation.surface: Joining up, an army recruit is welcomed by an officer with real panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' looks like enlisting, but 'Join' alone is the definition; UP goes inside COL plus E, the last letter of 'panache'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair two things together, such as railway carriages, is to link or connect them.

clue.text: Trail flighty daughter missing home, finally penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals in a pen, so the note goes inside the rearranged letters
flighty means fickle and unsettled, so the letters of the remaining word are rearranged
missing means the named letter is taken out of daughter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of home

explanation.surface: A giddy daughter who has left home, and finally writes a note while following a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing home, finally' takes E (the last letter of 'home') out of DAUGHTER; 'flighty' scrambles DAUGHTR, and 'penning' puts N inside to give the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of hunt follows an artificial scent dragged across country, so it follows a laid trail.

clue.text: Fighter lacerated or knocked over

parts.note: lacerated means tore, as of flesh

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means the word or is turned upside down, reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A boxer cut badly, or knocked down to the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boxer; the fighter is a Spanish bullfighter. 'knocked over' turns OR round to give RO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish term names a bullfighter, especially one on foot, so it is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: River Thames is improbably flowing west? Not totally

indicators.note: in an across clue flowing west means reading right to left, so the run of letters is read backwards
not totally means only part of these clue words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Doubting that the Thames could really flow westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SISI sit inside 'thameS IS Improbably'; 'flowing west' reads them right to left. The Isis is the stretch of the Thames at Oxford, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name used at Oxford for the upper reaches of the Thames, a river.

clue.text: Steps taken to avoid danger

parts.note: the steps are literal stairs, the outside metal staircase used to get out of a burning building

explanation.surface: Precautions someone takes to stay out of harm's way.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the outdoor staircase fitted to buildings for escaping a blaze.

clue.text: Leading light to join the Tories?

explanation.surface: A party newcomer hailed as a guiding figure for the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as BE A CON: to become a Conservative, CON being short for that party, nicknamed the Tories in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire or lighthouse guides people, a leading light; read as be-a-con, it means becoming a Conservative.

clue.text: Primate's correspondence containing a lot of mail from Germany

indicators.note: containing means the correspondence word holds the shortened German word inside it

parts.note: chime means agreement or correspondence, as when things chime with each other

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: Panzer is German for armour, mail being armour too

explanation.surface: A church leader's letters stuffed with post sent from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop and 'mail' letters, but mail is armour: PANZE(R) goes inside CHIME.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape of African forests is one of the primates, the order including monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Inspected one sheep kept by clergyman

indicators.note: kept by means the following pieces are held inside the clergyman's title

parts.note: Revd is the abbreviation for Reverend, the title of a clergyman
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A vicar who looks after a single sheep has looked it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To look something over carefully is to examine or assess it.

clue.text: Score increased by 50%

parts.note: a score is twenty, and half as much again makes ten more

explanation.surface: A team's tally going up by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a sports result, but it is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty plus half of twenty gives the number thirty.

clue.text: Massage initially cures the sore feet

indicators.note: to massage is to knead and work over, so these letters are worked into a new order
initially points to the first letter of cures

explanation.surface: A rubdown that soothes sore feet at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' looks like the body part being massaged, but it means metrical feet in poetry. C (first letter of 'cures') with THE SORE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are metrical units of a long syllable followed by a short one, and such units in verse are called feet.

clue.text: Appointment often linked with a title

definitions.text: Appointment often linked with a title

parts.words: Appointment often linked with a title
parts.note: the title is a newspaper or magazine name, and the job is running that publication

explanation.surface: A job that comes with a grand honorific attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title' suggests a rank like Sir or Lord, but here it is the name of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper holds a post tied to that paper's name.

clue.text: Consequences of a fall, multicoloured?

parts.note: the fall is rainfall, and sunlight through it makes coloured arcs in the sky

explanation.surface: Bruises after a tumble, turning all shades.
explanation.walkthrough: A fall suggests a tumble and multicoloured bruises; it is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured arcs appear in the sky when sunshine meets falling rain.

clue.text: Conspirator endlessly active, accepting monotonous routine

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened word takes the routine word inside it
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: busy means active
a rut is a dull, unchanging routine

explanation.surface: A plotter who is always busy despite a dull, repetitive life.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Brutus was one of the plotters who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Way to finish down and out?

definitions.text: Way to finish down and out?

parts.words: Way to finish down and out?
parts.note: down and out reads as homeless, but literally a hinged opening in a floor lets someone drop down and out, as on a gallows

explanation.surface: A route that ends in destitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down and out' suggests poverty; read literally it is falling through a hatch, as on a gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hatch in a floor or stage drops a person through it.

clue.text: One attacking assistant engaged by bishop

indicators.note: engaged by means taken on or held by, so the assistant goes inside the bishop's abbreviation

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assailant turns out to be a helper hired by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is the style of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries out a sudden attack or incursion is an attacker.

clue.text: Bulb needed in the kitchen

parts.note: bulb suggests a light bulb, but this is a pungent plant bulb used in cooking

explanation.surface: A light bulb wanted for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent plant grows as a bulb of cloves used to flavour food.

clue.text: Russian writer accepts round figure, very large

indicators.note: accepts means the writer's name takes the round letter inside it

parts.note: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A Russian author takes on a large round sum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the number ten to the hundredth power, an enormous figure.

clue.text: Chess manoeuvre, antic of the devious?

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tricky chess move, the sort of prank a sly player pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: This chess opening development places a bishop on the long diagonal, a standard move pattern.

clue.text: Woman's heartless game

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the game is removed

parts.note: rugby is a ball game

explanation.surface: A woman's game played without feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Area of jurisprudence, not civil

indicators.note: area of means a section of the word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A branch of law that is not civil law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not civil' suggests criminal law in the legal surface, but it means impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite behaviour is uncivil, lacking courtesy.

clue.text: Dangerous cut on side of eye

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: side of means one edge letter of eye is taken

explanation.surface: A risky wound next to someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave illness or harsh storm is serious and threatening.

clue.text: Appear depressed after confrontation

parts.note: to show up is to appear
down means depressed or sad

explanation.surface: Someone looks miserable after a bitter argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A final decisive clash between rivals is a face-off.
